Subject: Delgado Housing Case Strategy Conference Summary

Dear Delgado Housing Team,

Here is the summary of the Delgado Housing Case Strategy Conference held on April 29, 2026:

1. Evidence: The core exhibits will be the unit 4B repair log (23 entries since November), building management text messages (41 messages), and the Harbor County Code Enforcement inspection report from April 9 citing three violations (heat, leak, mold). Photos will be supporting evidence.

2. Answer and Counterclaim: We will file an answer with a habitability counterclaim against Maplewood Properties LLC seeking rent abatement from November 3, 2025, when the heat first failed. The draft will be prepared by Amara Singh and filed by May 6, 2026. Rosa Delgado will provide signed verification.

3. Rent Escrow: $4,200 will be deposited with Harbor County Housing Court. Rosa will obtain a money order on Friday and bring proof to the clinic. Kofi Mensah will track the deposit.

4. Hearing Timeline: The hearing is scheduled for May 14, 2026. The Tenant Mediation Program is declined unless repairs begin. Rosa will notify Kofi immediately if any repair crew arrives.

5. Check-ins: Weekly check-ins are set for Wednesdays at the same time through May 13.

6. Scope: The case focuses on the nonpayment defense and habitability counterclaim only. Other claims will be considered after the hearing.

7. Ongoing Evidence: Rosa will maintain a daily temperature log and continue taking dated photos. A request for a code enforcement re-inspection will be made.

Please let me know if you have any questions or need further details.

Best regards,
Amara Singh
Eastside Legal Aid Clinic

segments.text: Morning everyone — thanks for being on time. I want to keep us tight today, we've got four things to get through and I'd like to wrap by 11. Kofi, Rosa, you good to dive in?
Morning. Yep, ready.
Hi Amara, hi Kofi. Ready.

Great. Agenda: habitability evidence, the answer and counterclaim, rent escrow, hearing timeline. Let's start with the evidence. Rosa, you've been keeping the records — can you walk us through what we have?

So I have three main things. First is the unit 4B repair log I started in November — 23 entries now, the heat going out, the leak in the bathroom ceiling, the mold behind the tub. Second is the building management text messages, about 41 of them, and most of their replies are either nothing or 'we'll send someone.' Third is the Harbor County Code Enforcement inspection from April 9 — the inspector cited three violations, the heat, the leak, and the mold. I also have a lot of photos but the older ones don't have dates on them, and my neighbor in 4C said she might write a statement but she hasn't committed.

Yeah, I'd lead with the log, the texts, and the code enforcement report. The photos are fine as supporting material but without dates they won't carry much, and I wouldn't count on the neighbor statement.
Agreed. So the repair log, the texts, and the code enforcement report are our core exhibits, and the photos go in as supporting?
Yes, that makes sense to me.
Plus one.
Good. Decision: repair log, building management texts, and the code enforcement report are the core exhibits. Kofi, can you compile them into an exhibit set this week so I can review by Monday?
Will do. I'll have it in the case file by end of day Friday.
Perfect. Item two — the answer and counterclaim against Maplewood Properties LLC. I want to land on the scope today. Kofi, what's your read?

I've been going back and forth. If we only answer and deny the nonpayment claim, we're just playing defense. I'd file the answer with a habitability counterclaim asking for rent abatement going back to November, when the heat first failed. That's a strong enough period to matter, and the log and the inspection back it up.

I agree with that. And on the dates — the heat first went out November 3, the ceiling leak started in early January, and the mold showed up after that. I wrote each one down the day it happened, so the log lines up.
That works for me. Any concern about claiming back to November when the texts to building management only start in December?
Some, but the November 3 log entry notes she called the office that day. I think it's worth claiming the full period and letting the landlord argue it down.

Okay. Decision: we file the answer with a habitability counterclaim against Maplewood Properties LLC seeking abatement from November. I'll draft it, and we file by May 6. Kofi, you'll get Rosa's signed verification once the draft is ready?
Yep.
Good. Item three — rent escrow. Daniel confirmed the $4,200 figure last week. Rosa, how do you want to handle the deposit?

I've been setting the rent aside since February like you told me, so I have it. I can get a money order from my credit union on Friday morning for the full $4,200 and bring it to the Harbor County Housing Court clerk the same day. Then I'll bring the receipt and a copy of the money order to the clinic so it's in the file.
That works. I'd just flag that the $4,200 assumes the court doesn't ask for May's rent to be added before the hearing — if it does, that number goes up.

Noted. We can revisit if the clerk raises it. Decision: $4,200 deposited in escrow with Harbor County Housing Court, Rosa brings the money order proof to the clinic. Kofi, please track the deposit in the case file today.
On it.

Last item — hearing timeline. I want to be thoughtful here, because Maplewood's counsel floated the Tenant Mediation Program. If we agree too quickly we lose leverage, and if we refuse outright the court may see us as unreasonable. Where do we land?

My preference is to keep the May 14 hearing. They've promised me repairs three times since November and nothing happened. If they actually start fixing things, then I'd be willing to talk in mediation.
I like that. Mediation hasn't gone well with this landlord on the last two cases we had against them.
Agreed. Decision: we proceed to the May 14 hearing and decline the Tenant Mediation Program unless repairs actually begin. Rosa, you'll tell Kofi right away if any repair crew shows up?
Yes.
And Kofi, you'll coordinate with Hannah on docketing the filing deadline and the hearing date, since she's lining up the filing packet?
Yep, I'll loop Hannah in this week.

Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items — Rosa: money order and escrow deposit Friday, proof to the clinic, tell Kofi about any repairs. Kofi: exhibit set by Friday, escrow tracking today, signed verification, docketing with Hannah. Me: I'll draft the answer and counterclaim for filing by May 6 and update Daniel on the plan. Anything I'm missing?
I think that covers it.
One thing — do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and May 14? I'd suggest weekly given how much we have to land before the hearing.
Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through May 13.
Works.
Works.

One more thing while I have you both — on scope, are we still aligned that this case is the nonpayment defense and the habitability counterclaim, and that a separate repair action or a retaliation claim waits until after the hearing? I don't want us to take on more than we can prove by May 14.
Understood. Just the defense and counterclaim for now. If things get worse after the hearing we can talk about the rest then.
Same.

Great. And on what we keep building before the hearing — updated dated photos of the ceiling and the tub, and a request for a code enforcement re-inspection. Anything else you think we should capture?
I could keep a daily temperature log with the thermometer Kofi gave me — just the morning and evening reading, every day until the hearing.
Plus one on that. Easy to do, and judges like it.
Added. So ongoing evidence: dated photos, re-inspection request, daily temperature log. Rosa, please start the temperature log tonight and bring it to next Wednesday's check-in.
Will do.
Okay — anything else for either of you before I let you go?
Nothing from me.
Nothing here.
Okay, I think that's everything on my list — let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused.
Thanks Amara — good session.
Yes, thank you both. Talk soon!
Alright, I've got to jump to my 11 — talk soon.
Heads up if you're coming in Friday — the elevator at the clinic is out again. They say it'll be fixed by next week, but I wouldn't count on it.
That's okay, it's only the second floor. I'm used to stairs with our building anyway.
Friday walk-in hours are nine to noon. If you come for the drop-off, just tell the front desk you're there to see me.
I'll come early. Last time I came on a Friday the line was out the door by ten.
Good idea. And parking out front is a mess right now — they tore up the lot on the side for repaving, so it's all meters on the street.
I'll take the bus then. The 14 stops right on the corner after the credit union.
That's probably easier. I circled for fifteen minutes on Monday before I found a spot.
Ha. That's why I gave up on driving downtown a long time ago.
Anyway. Bring your ID Friday — the front desk started signing everyone in. Anything else on your mind before I hop off?
Actually, yes. There's something else, but it's not about the apartment.
My ex filed for custody of my daughter in Harbor County Family Court last week. I got served on Saturday. The papers say I have to file a response by May 20.

And the thing is, there was a protective-order case in 2019 — I filed it against him and then withdrew it before the hearing. I never told anyone here about it, it's not in my intake. I don't know if it helps me or hurts me now.
Okay. Thank you for telling me. Does his petition mention the 2019 case at all?

No, not at all. His lawyer made it sound like I'm the unstable one because of the housing case. I have my daughter's school attendance records and her pediatrician records showing I take her to every appointment — I was thinking of submitting those with my response.
Those records could matter a lot. I'm not on the family-law side, though, so I don't want to steer you wrong on what to file — especially on whether to bring up the 2019 order.
Honestly, can we keep this between us for now? I haven't decided what to do about the protective order, and I don't want everyone at the clinic knowing about it before I do.
Understood. What I can do is ask Daniel whether the clinic can take it or refer you to a family-law attorney — just that you have a custody response due May 20, nothing more.
That would help. I can't afford a private lawyer on top of everything else.
There are a couple of family-law programs that take referrals from us. Bring the petition with you Friday so whoever takes it can see the deadline, and the school and medical records too.
Okay. Could we talk more about it before Friday? I'm nervous about the deadline.
Of course. Thursday afternoon call?
Thursday works. I'll call the clinic line.
Okay, I should head out — see you Friday at walk-in hours.
Okay, take care. Thank you, Kofi.
